payload.title: The knock at the door

payload.name: The Shulammite
payload.note: The dark but lovely bride of the Song of Solomon who speaks most of the Song; keeper of her brothers' vineyards. Distinct from the figurative bride of Revelation.

stages.label: The Shulammite

quotes.quote: Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is as a flock of goats, that descend from Mount Gilead.
with one chain of your neck.

stages.text: The Shulammite: a young woman of about eighteen to twenty; slender, graceful build; warm dark skin tanned by sun from working the vineyards; long dark hair, thick and flowing like goats descending Gilead, often partly veiled; large dove-like dark eyes, soft gaze, full lips, a fine chain at her neck; signature outfit a plain undyed linen tunic with a deep red woven wrap-cloak; signature prop a small wooden basket or a sprig of henna blossom.

payload.name: The beloved shepherd (Song of Solomon)
payload.note: The bride's young shepherd lover who browses among lilies and tends flocks, distinct from King Solomon and from the teacher in Ecclesiastes.

stages.label: The beloved shepherd

quotes.quote: My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.
My beloved is like a roe or a young deer.
My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

stages.text: The beloved shepherd: a young man of about twenty, lean and sure-footed from the hills, with a ruddy, sun-browned skin and dark curly hair cut just above the shoulders, a short dark beard, and clear, steady eyes. His signature outfit is a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown, belted with a leather cord, and a rough dark-grey wool cloak. He carries a shepherd's crook of pale wood.

payload.name: Mother's house (Song of Solomon)
payload.note: The bride's mother's house where the lover wishes to bring her.

stages.label: Mother's house

quotes.quote: I would lead you, bringing you into the house of my mother, who would instruct me.
I would have you drink spiced wine, of the juice of my pomegranate.

stages.text: Mother's house: a modest village dwelling of pale limestone and mud brick under a flat roof, with a low doorway of dark timber and a courtyard wall. A pomegranate tree grows beside the house, heavy with fruit, and terraced vineyards and olive groves lie on the slopes behind it. Clay jars and a stone grinding place stand in the courtyard.

payload.title: Regular and feast offerings

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
payload.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
payload.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

payload.name: Moses
payload.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
payload.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
payload.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

aliases: the mountain that might be touched
payload.name: Horeb/Mount Sinai
payload.note: The single mountain of God where the law and covenant are given; all listed entries (Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Malachi, Hebrews) refer to the same mountain under the names Horeb, Sinai, God's mountain, referenced across divisions.

stages.label: Horeb/Mount Sinai

quotes.quote: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire
You shall set bounds to the people all around
the cloud covered it six days
The mountain burned with fire to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

stages.text: Horeb/Mount Sinai: a single steep granite mountain rising from a stark desert wilderness of rock and sand; its lower slopes are broken boulders and gravel, its upper peak sharp and dark, with a cloud-wrapped summit. The base is marked by a rocky plain where the people camp, bounded by stones. No vegetation beyond scattered desert shrub; the mountain has no buildings.

payload.title: Sons of Israel and the families of Judah and Caleb
Raising Jairus's daughter

aliases: the apostle and high priest of our confession
the great shepherd of the sheep
the author and perfecter of faith
the mediator of a new covenant
the Lion of the tribe of Judah
the rider called Faithful and True
KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS
payload.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord
payload.note: The one Jesus: the teacher from Nazareth of the Gospels and Acts, and the risen, exalted Christ and Lord of the epistles and Revelation; the same individual across all divisions, with death, resurrection and changed portrayal not creating new individuals.

stages.label: Adult Jesus

quotes.quote: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

stages.text: Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

stages.label: Infant Jesus

quotes.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

payload.name: Jairus, synagogue ruler
payload.note: Synagogue ruler whose daughter Jesus raises from the dead, appearing in Matthew, Mark-style narrative and Luke 8; the father pleading for his daughter.

stages.label: Jairus, synagogue ruler

quotes.quote: one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name, came; and seeing him, he fell at his feet
He was a ruler of the synagogue. He fell down at Jesus’ feet and begged him to come into his house

stages.text: Jairus: a man of about fifty, of middle height and sturdy build, with olive skin weathered by the sun, short dark hair and a close-trimmed grey-streaked beard, a lined, earnest face and dark, anxious eyes. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic to the knee under a dark blue-brown woollen cloak with tasselled hem. He carries no props of his own.

payload.name: Jairus's daughter
payload.note: Twelve-year-old girl raised from apparent death by Jesus in Mark, also called Talitha; a girl, distinct from the Shunammite's son.

stages.label: Jairus's daughter

quotes.quote: Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha cumi!”
The child is not dead, but is asleep.

stages.text: Jairus's daughter: a girl of about twelve; slender, small-boned build; olive skin; dark hair worn long and loose, bound with a simple cord; gentle, pale-lipped face with dark eyes. Wears a plain undyed linen tunic to the ankles in soft ochre, with a faded blue wrap over the shoulders. No props.

payload.name: Simon Peter
payload.note: The fisherman apostle, first-called disciple and leader of the twelve, who appears in the Gospels, Acts, Galatians and both letters of Peter; all entries here are the same individual, distinguished only by role and portrayal.

stages.label: Simon Peter

quotes.quote: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas

stages.text: Simon Peter: a sturdy man in his thirties, broad-shouldered from hauling nets, weathered brown skin from sun on the Sea of Galilee, short dark curly hair and a full beard flecked with grey. Plain undyed tunic of natural linen under a rough brown wool cloak. Signature props: a coiled fishing net over one shoulder and a wooden fishing staff.

payload.name: James son of Zebedee
payload.note: Fisherman disciple called with his brother John in Matthew; distinct from James son of Alphaeus.

stages.label: James son of Zebedee

quotes.quote: James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets.
James the son of Zebedee; and John, the brother of James, (whom he called Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder);

stages.text: James son of Zebedee: a man in his late twenties to thirties; lean, strong build from hauling nets; weathered olive-brown skin; short dark curly hair and a close-trimmed beard; steady, earnest eyes and a sun-lined face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre-brown with a dark wool cloak in faded blue-grey. Carries a coiled fishing net over one shoulder.

payload.name: John son of Zebedee
payload.note: Fisherman, son of Zebedee and brother of James, one of the inner three in Mark; not the Baptizer.

stages.label: John son of Zebedee

quotes.quote: he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who were also in the boat mending the nets.
(whom he called Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder)

stages.text: John son of Zebedee: a young man in his twenties, lean and strong from work on the lake; olive-brown skin; dark curly hair cut at the neck, with a short, close beard; weathered, steady face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic in earthy brown, belted, with a dark wool cloak in deep blue-grey. No props carried alone.

payload.name: the synagogue (Mark)
payload.note: The Jewish meeting house in Mark's Gospel where Jesus teaches, heals and exorcises; the Capernaum, Nazareth and Jairus scenes all set here.

stages.label: the synagogue (Mark)

quotes.quote: They went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.

stages.text: the synagogue: a modest stone meeting house of Galilean Judea, low walls of dressed limestone, a flat roof on timber beams, and a deep porch with wide stone steps. Inside, a raised platform and a cabinet for the scrolls face rows of plain stone benches. Olive and fig trees shade the courtyard; a stone-paved street runs beside it.

aliases: the court of the high priest
the courtyard of the high priest
payload.name: the court of the high priest (Caiaphas)
payload.note: Courtyard of Caiaphas where Jesus is tried and Peter denies him in Matthew; same court as the high priest's court in John, identified by Caiaphas and the trial setting.

stages.label: The court of the high priest

quotes.quote: the court of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas
He was sitting with the officers, and warming himself in the light of the fire.
entered in with Jesus into the court of the high priest

stages.text: The court of the high priest: an open paved courtyard of pale limestone flagstones inside a high-walled stone house in Jerusalem. A wide arched gateway with a timber door faces the street. A charcoal fire burns on a stone hearth at the centre of the court, and a stone porch with columns stands along one side. Olive and fig trees grow in clay pots by the walls; the upper walls are plastered and lit by torch sconces.

payload.title: The queen recalls Daniel

payload.name: The queen (queen mother of Belshazzar)
payload.note: Unnamed queen in Belshazzar's time who recalls Daniel's wisdom from Nebuchadnezzar's reign; a separate figure from Esther and from the Sheba queen.

stages.label: The queen, queen mother

quotes.quote: The queen by reason of the words of the king and his lords came into the banquet house.

stages.text: The queen: a woman of about fifty to sixty, of medium height and dignified carriage; olive-toned skin; dark hair, grey at the temples, drawn back under a sheer veil and a gold-banded diadem; a calm, lined face with steady dark eyes. Her signature outfit is a long deep-purple court robe with gold embroidery at the hem and sleeves, over a cream linen undergarment. Her only prop is a slender gold-capped ivory staff.

payload.name: Belshazzar
payload.note: King of Babylon during the feast and handwriting on the wall; slain the same night.

stages.label: Belshazzar, king of Babylon

quotes.quote: Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords
his face was changed in him

stages.text: Belshazzar: a man in his thirties or early forties, of lean, upright build; olive-bronze skin; short dark hair and a neatly curled beard in the Mesopotamian royal manner; a strong brow and deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long fringed royal robe of deep crimson wool over a white linen tunic, with a tall, pleated, gold-banded crown. Carries a gold-hilted ceremonial dagger at the belt.

payload.name: Royal palace of Babylon
payload.note: Babylonian palace where the king receives counsel, sees the handwriting and hears Daniel's interpretations; distinct from the Susa palace.

stages.label: Royal palace of Babylon

quotes.quote: he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon

stages.text: Royal palace of Babylon: a vast walled complex on the flat alluvial plain of the Euphrates, built of sun-dried and fired brick glazed in deep blue with yellow lion and dragon reliefs. Tiered terraces rise toward a great gate with tall towers; hanging gardens of palms, date trees and climbing vines spill over the walls. Broad courts of pale stone lead to a banquet hall with high cedar-beamed ceilings and a river-facing colonnade.

payload.title: Love your enemies; judging others

payload.name: Crowd in Luke
payload.note: The mass of people following Jesus, hearing John and being healed throughout Luke.

stages.label: Crowd in Luke

quotes.quote: a great number of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon
A great multitude of the people followed him, including women who also mourned and lamented him.

stages.text: Crowd in Luke: a typical member is an ordinary adult of Judean or Galilean village life, from young adult to middle age, lean and sun-worn, with olive or brown skin, dark hair kept short or tied back, and a short beard or clean-shaven face; plain undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, undyed cream and earth brown, with a woollen cloak and a head covering; carries no props of their own.

payload.name: Galilee
payload.note: The northern region of Galilee where Jesus preaches, teaches and heals; both Matthew and Luke describe the same region, so these entries are one place.

stages.label: Galilee

quotes.quote: Walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers
teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom
toward the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles

stages.text: Galilee: Northern hill country falling to a freshwater lake, the sea of Galilee, its shore lined with fishing boats and nets drying on stone. Low limestone villages of flat-roofed houses, a white stone synagogue with a shallow portico, terraced olive groves, fig trees and scrubland. Roman roads and a distant Gentile town on the slopes.

payload.title: Proverbs on the tongue, pride and friendship

payload.name: Solomon
payload.note: Son of David and Bathsheba, king of Israel who builds the temple; the same individual across all divisions. Distinguish from the Shulammite's shepherd beloved, who is not Solomon.

stages.label: Solomon, king of Israel

quotes.quote: had Solomon ride on King David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon.
sat down on his throne and caused a throne to be set for the king’s mother

stages.text: Solomon: man in his twenties to forties, lean and upright with a composed, dignified bearing; warm olive-brown skin; dark curly hair and a short, neatly trimmed beard; calm, thoughtful face with a broad brow. Signature outfit: a long deep-blue royal court robe with gold-thread borders over a white linen tunic, and a gold circlet on his head. Signature prop: a plain rod of royal authority carried alone.

payload.title: The vision of the four living creatures and the glory of Yahweh

payload.name: Ezekiel son of Buzi
payload.note: Exiled priest and prophet at the river Chebar.

stages.label: Ezekiel son of Buzi

quotes.quote: Yahweh’s word came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar

stages.text: Ezekiel son of Buzi: a man of about thirty, lean and steady, with dark hair and a short trimmed beard, bronze-brown skin from desert sun, and a calm, watchful face. He wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic with a long cloak of rough brown wool over it. He carries a wooden writing tablet and stylus.

payload.name: Four living creatures
payload.note: Winged beings with four faces (man, lion, ox, eagle) who bear the divine throne in Ezekiel 1 and 10; cherubim by alias but not the Psalms angels.

stages.label: Four living creatures

quotes.quote: Out of its center came the likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: They had the likeness of a man.
their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches.
The appearance of the wheels was like a beryl stone.
The form of a man’s hand appeared here in the cherubim under their wings.

stages.text: Four living creatures: adult beings of ageless bearing; each has the likeness of a man in form, with four faces of man, lion, ox and eagle, and four wings. Skin is bronze-gold, burnished like coals; hair fine and flowing; eyes bright as torchlight. One signature outfit: no garment, only the wings and the bright radiance of fire about them, colours of gold, bronze and smoky flame. Signature prop: none, but each bears a wheel like beryl stone beside it.

payload.name: River Chebar
payload.note: The river in Babylonia where the exiles dwell and Ezekiel receives his visions, call and commissions; distinct from the Ahava, which is Ezra's gathering point.

stages.label: River Chebar

quotes.quote: as I was among the captives by the river Chebar
in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar
the captivity at Tel Aviv who lived by the river Chebar

stages.text: River Chebar: a slow, broad canal-river of the Babylonian plain, its brown-green water running between low earthen banks lined with reeds, date palms and willows. Mud-brick and fired-brick settlements of the exile stand on rising ground above the flood line, with irrigation channels, earthen dykes and walled fields stretching flat to the horizon.

payload.title: Plans for the bronze altar and the court
Request of James and John

payload.name: James and John, sons of Zebedee
payload.note: Two brothers, disciples of Jesus, who ask for seats at his right and left and later fish with Peter at the lake; both entries describe this same pair, so they are one cluster.

stages.label: James and John, sons of Zebedee

quotes.quote: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came near to him
the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together

stages.text: James and John, sons of Zebedee: young men in their twenties, lean and weathered from lake work; brown skin, dark curly hair cut short above the ears, closely trimmed beards; sun-creased faces, steady eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic in earth brown with a rough wool cloak in faded blue-grey. Signature prop: a coiled fishing net slung over one shoulder.

payload.name: The Twelve Disciples (collective)
payload.note: The twelve apostles/disciples as one collective body acting together across the Gospels and Acts; distinct from the individual disciples named within them.

stages.label: The Twelve Disciples (collective)

quotes.quote: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, who is called Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee
One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,

stages.text: The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.

payload.name: Jericho
payload.note: The one walled city of Jericho in the Bible; all six entries describe this same place in Joshua, 2 Kings, the Gospels and Hebrews, so they are one cluster.

stages.label: Jericho, the city of palms

quotes.quote: Now Jericho was tightly shut up because of the children of Israel. No one went out, and no one came in.
going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell down after they had been encircled for seven days.
With the loss of his firstborn he will lay its foundation, and with the loss of his youngest son he will set up its gates.

stages.text: Jericho: a walled city on the plains beside the Jordan, near the Dead Sea, with broad flat terrain of sun-bleached earth and sparse scrub. Tall date palms rise among the houses and gardens, and mud-brick and stone walls ring the city, with a heavy timber-and-stone gate. Limestone hills climb westward behind it toward the hill country, with a rough road cut into the slope.

payload.title: Request for prayer and the Lord's faithfulness

aliases: my child's father in the faith
the aged prisoner of Christ Jesus
payload.name: Paul the apostle
payload.note: The apostle Paul, author and speaker of all thirteen letters; the same individual across Romans, Corinthians, Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians, Thessalonians, Timothy, Titus and Philemon, identified by his apostolic authorship and first-person voice.

stages.label: Paul the apostle

quotes.quote: being such a one as Paul, the aged, but also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains.
I, Paul, write this with my own hand

stages.text: Paul the apostle: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifties to sixties, wiry and weathered from travel and imprisonment; Jewish Mediterranean features, olive-brown skin, short greying-dark beard and close-cropped hair receding at the temples; lined brow, steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark-blue cloak. Signature prop: a rolled parchment scroll and a reed pen case at the belt.

payload.name: Silas (Silvanus)
payload.note: Jerusalem brother and companion of Paul in Acts and the letters, also named Silvanus in the epistles; all four entries are the same missionary companion, so join them into one cluster.

stages.label: Silas (Silvanus), missionary companion

quotes.quote: Silas, chief men among the brothers.
Judas and Silas, also being prophets themselves

stages.text: Silas (Silvanus): a man in his thirties, of medium height and sturdy build from travel. Olive skin, dark curly hair cropped short above the ears, a close-cut beard. Calm, steady eyes and a weathered, earnest face. Wears a plain undyed linen tunic with a dark brown woollen cloak thrown over the shoulders. Carries a traveller's leather satchel and a wooden staff.

payload.name: Timothy
payload.note: Paul's young companion and fellow worker, the son of Eunice from Lystra, who appears in Acts, the letters co-sent with Paul, and the two pastoral letters addressed to him; all twelve entries are the same man.

stages.label: Timothy

quotes.quote: a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a Jewess who believed, but his father was a Greek.

stages.text: Timothy: a young man of about twenty to twenty-five; slender, medium build; olive-brown skin; short dark curly hair and a smooth, clean-shaven face; calm, earnest features. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a dark brown woollen cloak. He carries a traveller's leather satchel and walking staff.

payload.name: the Thessalonians
payload.note: The believing assembly at Thessalonica addressed as brothers and sisters in both letters; the same collective recipients, so the two entries are one cluster.

stages.label: the Thessalonians

quotes.quote: to the assembly of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
working night and day, that we might not burden any of you

stages.text: The Thessalonians: a typical member is an adult of 25 to 50 years, working people of a Macedonian port city; olive to tan skin; short-cropped or tied-back dark hair, men clean-shaven or with short beards; calm, earnest, weathered faces. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a dark brown woollen cloak, sandals.

payload.name: Thessalonica
payload.note: The city in Macedonia with a Jewish synagogue, visited by Paul and Silas in Acts, addressed as the recipient church in 1 and 2 Thessalonians, and named as Demas's destination in 2 Timothy; all four entries are the same city.

stages.label: Thessalonica

quotes.quote: they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

stages.text: Thessalonica: a bustling Roman port city on the curved shore of the Thermaic Gulf, backed by green hills and Mount Olympus visible far to the southwest. Pale limestone and brick houses climb terraced slopes, with tiled roofs and a grid of stone-paved streets. A Roman forum with colonnades, a stone-built synagogue with a plain facade, and a harbour of moored fishing boats and merchant ships; olive trees and cypresses along the walls.

payload.title: Hananiah breaks the yoke

payload.name: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah
payload.note: Prophet from Anathoth who speaks most of the book.

stages.label: Jeremiah

quotes.quote: The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
They let down Jeremiah with cords. In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire.

stages.text: Jeremiah: a man in his middle years, lean and weathered from long journeys and imprisonment, with a grave, careworn face and deep-set dark eyes. Close-cropped dark hair and a short greying beard. Dark-skinned Levantine complexion. Wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic under a long brown wool cloak, the cloak worn thin at the hem. Carries a plain wooden staff.

payload.name: Hananiah son of Azzur
payload.note: False prophet who breaks Jeremiah's yoke.

stages.label: Hananiah son of Azzur

quotes.quote: Hananiah the son of Azzur, the prophet, who was of Gibeon

stages.text: Hananiah son of Azzur: man in his middle years, lean and upright, of Israelite Levantine type with a dignified bearing. Skin olive-brown, weathered by travel. Dark hair and a short trimmed beard streaked with grey. Strong brow, intent dark eyes, a stern and earnest face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a deep ochre prophet's cloak with a woven band at the hem. Carries a plain wooden staff of olive wood.

aliases: the house which is called by my name
the tent of the daughter of Zion
the house of Yahweh of Armies
payload.name: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple)
payload.note: The one Jerusalem temple (Yahweh's house, the sanctuary on Mount Moriah) across all references, from Solomon's building through repair, destruction and rebuilding; construction and ruin are later appearance stages, not separate places.

stages.label: Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah

quotes.quote: The house, when it was under construction, was built of stone prepared at the quarry
Within the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
Also he made before the house two pillars thirty-five cubits high
He set the sea on the right side of the house eastward and toward the south.

stages.text: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

payload.title: Temple sermon
Proverbs on the city, the righteous and the wicked
Praise for Yahweh's acts in history

payload.name: The righteous (Psalms)
payload.note: The collective of the godly and humble who trust Yahweh and suffer oppression across the Psalms; distinct from the remnant of Judah, which is a specific Judahite community addressed by Zephaniah.

stages.label: The righteous (Psalms)

quotes.quote: My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.
For the needy shall not always be forgotten, nor the hope of the poor perish forever.
He raises up the poor out of the dust, and lifts up the needy from the ash heap,

stages.text: The righteous: adults of mixed age, mostly middle-aged, lean and sturdy from farm and road labour; olive to brown skin; dark hair kept short or tied back, men with trimmed beards; plain, careworn faces, dignified and steady. Signature outfit: undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre and earth tones with a plain brown woollen cloak. Signature prop: a simple staff or walking stick.

payload.name: Egypt
payload.note: The land of Egypt where patriarchs sojourn, Israel is enslaved and plagues fall; recurs in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Psalms, Ezekiel, Hosea, Micah and Hebrews as the same land.

stages.label: Egypt

quotes.quote: The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dwell in the best of the land.
Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen
But the midwives feared God, and didn’t do what the king of Egypt commanded them
for Memphis will become a desolation, and will be burned up, without inhabitant.

stages.text: Egypt: a long green valley of the Nile flanked by pale desert; broad river channels, canals and reed marsh; fertile black earth fields of barley and flax; date palms and sycamores; mud-brick and limestone cities with tall temple pylons, obelisks and fortified walls; the Delta with its towns of Goshen and Zoan.

payload.title: Whose son is the Christ; warning against scribes

payload.name: the scribes
payload.note: Teachers of the law who question and oppose Jesus in Matthew and Luke; the Matthew and Luke entries describe the same scribal opposition and are joined.

stages.label: the scribes

quotes.quote: Beware of those scribes who like to walk in long robes
The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat.

stages.text: the scribes: men of middle to advanced age, lean and upright, of Judean build; olive skin, dark close-cropped or short-bearded hair, lined faces; a typical member wears a long undyed linen tunic under a dark wool cloak with long fringed tassels at the hem and phylacteries bound on the brow and left arm; sober dark blue and brown tones; often carries a small rolled scroll of the law.

payload.name: the Jerusalem temple
payload.note: The single Jerusalem temple building across all five divisions (courts, porch and gates are parts of the same place), so every entry is one place.

stages.label: The Jerusalem temple

quotes.quote: Jesus entered into the temple of God and drove out all of those who sold and bought in the temple
The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom.
the door of the temple which is called Beautiful
how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts
His disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.

stages.text: The Jerusalem temple: a vast complex of white limestone and gleaming gold on a raised stone platform atop Mount Moriah. Wide colonnaded courts, a tall sanctuary house with a gilded roof, a great curtained veil within, a treasury chamber, and a Beautiful Gate of bronze. Olive trees and cedar frame the courts.

payload.title: Barnabas brings Saul to the apostles

payload.name: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)
payload.note: Pharisee from Tarsus who persecutes the Way, is converted on the road to Damascus, and becomes the apostle Paul; told apart from the king by his Pharisee and Tarsus background and conversion narrative in Acts.

stages.label: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)

quotes.quote: The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees.
But I was born a Roman.

stages.text: Saul/Paul: man in his thirties to fifties, middle height and spare, wiry build worn by travel and hardship. Olive-brown skin, dark hair cropped short, close-trimmed dark beard with grey beginning at the chin. Lined forehead, deep-set dark eyes, strong nose. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark brown travelling cloak with a fringed hem. Signature prop: a worn leather writing satchel and a plain wooden walking staff.

payload.name: Barnabas
payload.note: Levite of Cyprus, also called Joses, who travels with Paul.

stages.label: Barnabas

quotes.quote: a Levite, a man of Cyprus by race

stages.text: Barnabas: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and steady, with a weathered olive-brown skin from sea and road. Short dark hair going grey at the temples, and a neatly trimmed dark beard. Calm, warm eyes and a broad, open face. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long cream-brown wool cloak. Carries a worn leather travelling satchel and a wooden staff.

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
payload.name: Jerusalem
payload.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

payload.title: Proverbs on fools and the malicious
Red heifer and water of purification

payload.name: Aaron, brother of Moses
payload.note: Moses' older brother and first high priest, in Exodus and in Numbers (census, offerings, death on Mount Hor); the same man across both divisions.

stages.label: Aaron, the first high priest

quotes.quote: Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses.
Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, they made finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron
Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

stages.text: Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.

aliases: the sons of Aaron who were left
payload.name: Eleazar son of Aaron
payload.note: Third son of Aaron, later priest who oversees Levite duties and succeeds Aaron.

stages.label: Eleazar, priest

quotes.quote: that they make Aaron’s garments to sanctify him, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office.
Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priest’s office in the presence of Aaron their father.

stages.text: Eleazar: a man in his middle years, sturdy and dignified; olive-brown skin weathered by desert sun; short dark beard streaked with early grey; a calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. His signature outfit is a white linen priestly tunic with a blue-violet woven robe and a fine embroidered sash, a linen turban. He carries a bronze censer or a priest's staff.

payload.title: Healing of the lame man at the temple gate

payload.name: John the apostle, son of Zebedee
payload.note: Fisherman apostle, brother of James son of Zebedee, appearing in Matthew, Luke and Acts; distinct from John the Baptist and John Mark.

stages.label: John the apostle

quotes.quote: in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets
who were partners with Simon

stages.text: John the apostle: young man of about twenty-five to thirty; lean, strong fisherman's build; sun-browned skin; dark brown hair falling to the shoulders, short beard; clear, earnest eyes and a steady, youthful face. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in earth tones with a dark brown wool cloak, sleeves rolled. Carries a coiled fishing net over one shoulder.

payload.name: Crowd in Acts
payload.note: The crowd gathering in Jerusalem, Ephesus, Lystra and elsewhere to hear, mock or riot in Acts.

stages.label: Crowd in Acts

quotes.quote: the multitude came together and were bewildered, because everyone heard them speaking in his own language.
for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”

stages.text: Crowd in Acts: a typical member is an adult of about twenty to fifty years, lean and sun-browned from working outdoors, with dark brown or black hair worn short or tied back and beards kept short on men. Skin olive to tawny, faces weathered and serious. Clothing: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre or earth-brown, a dark wool cloak in deep blue or grey, sandals. Carries no props of his own.

payload.title: Circumcision of Abraham's household

aliases: Abraham the father of many nations
payload.name: Abram
payload.note: Son of Terah from Ur, called to Canaan and renamed Abraham; the same patriarch as Galatians' Abraham, so both entries form one cluster.

stages.label: Abram / Abraham

quotes.quote: Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
Abraham was one hundred years old when his son, Isaac, was born to him.
Abraham gave up his spirit, and died at a good old age, an old man, and full of years
Lot went with him.

stages.text: Abram, later Abraham: an elderly man of seventy-five to one hundred years and beyond; lean, weathered build from years of travel; dark skin tanned by desert sun; short greying beard and hair; deep-set, steady eyes and lined face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed wool wrap over a earth-brown linen tunic, leather sandals. Signature prop: a long wooden herder's staff.

payload.name: Ishmael son of Abraham
payload.note: Son of Abram and Hagar, cast out with his mother in Genesis; ancestor of twelve princes. Not the same as the later Ishmael son of Nethaniah.

stages.label: Ishmael, young son of Abraham

quotes.quote: Ishmael, his son, was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their villages, and by their encampments: twelve princes, according to their nations.

stages.text: Ishmael: a youth of about thirteen, slim and sturdy from desert work; warm brown skin; close-cropped dark hair and a thin young beard; a grave, watchful face with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen wrap and tunic in ochre-brown, with leather sandals. He carries a simple wooden bow and a leather quiver of arrows alone.

aliases: the hill country of the Amorites
payload.name: Canaan
payload.note: The promised land of Israel as a whole, the land Yahweh gives to Abram's descendants, referred to in Genesis, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Judges and Hebrews alike; all six entries describe this same land.

stages.label: Canaan, the promised land

quotes.quote: Surely it flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
Behold, Yahweh your God has set the land before you.
to the Western Sea
the land where you are traveling, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession
seven nations greater and mightier than you

stages.text: Canaan: a fertile hill country between the Jordan river and the Western Sea, with terraced slopes, olive groves, vineyards heavy with grapes, wheat fields in the valleys, and wells beside walled mud-brick and stone towns on the hilltops. Scattered oaks and terebinths mark old sacred places, and herders' pastures roll toward the distant coast.
